column1: # P. aeruginosa resistance mechanism knowledge table
# EDITABLE REFERENCE TABLE - not hard-coded in any analysis script.
# mechanism        : mechanism class assigned to the gene
# gene             : gene/locus name (must match the AMR or regulator table)
# antibiotic       : antibiotic(s) the mechanism is relevant to ("all" = any configured antibiotic)
# biological_role  : plain-language role, no causal claim
# evidence_level   : CEILING on the claim a raw detection of this gene can support.
#                    A detected gene can never exceed DETECTED. ASSOCIATED requires
#                    a statistical association in this cohort; SUPPORTED requires
#                    association plus consistent phenotype plus phylogenetic
#                    robustness. No row may be set to a causal claim.
# claim_ceiling    : strongest ClaimStatus a detection alone may reach
# notes            : caveats, direction of effect, assessment limits
# OprD context: OprD is the principal outer-membrane porin through which
# carbapenems enter. Loss of OprD reduces permeability. A detection of oprD
# sequence similarity is NOT a detection of OprD loss; the regulator/SV stage
# supplies that. The two are deliberately kept as separate mechanisms.
# The `antibiotic` column accepts a comma-separated list, so one row can cover
# every antibiotic a locus is relevant to. This is the mechanism by which a
# new antibiotic is added without editing any code: add it to config.yaml and
# to config/antibiotics.tsv, then extend the antibiotic column of the loci

column5: biological_role
column10: notes

column5: Outer-membrane porin; loss reduces carbapenem influx
column10: Presence of oprD indicates an intact locus, not susceptibility. Loss-of-function must come from stage 6 or stage 7. Same locus also affects other carbapenems.

column5: Repressor of the mexAB-opmD operon; alteration can de-repress efflux
column10: Direction of effect is context dependent in the literature. Report the variant, not a resistance call.

column5: Component of the MexXY/OprM pump machinery
column10: nalC loss-of-function variants are reported. Do not assume gain of resistance from detection alone.

column5: Component of the MexXY/OprM pump machinery
column10: Same caveats as nalC.

column5: Repressor of the mexXY operon
column10: Promoter and coding variants both relevant; promoter calls gated by config.

column5: Repressor of the mexXY operon
column10: Common site ofcarbapenem-associated regulatory variation.

column5: Positive regulator of the mexXY operon
column10: Usually an IS-associated insertion; see structural_variants stage.

column5: Secondary regulator of the mexXY operon
column10: Reported as a regulatory variant; direction not assumed.

column5: Peptidoglycan hydrolase that de-represses ampC transcription
column10: AmpC overproduction is the classical chromosomal route; this table records the locus, not the phenotype.

column5: Transcriptional regulator of the ampC operon
column10: AmpR also senses cell-wall precursors; effect direction is not assumed.

column5: D-alanyl-D-alanine carboxypeptidase; loss can affect cell-wall remodelling
column10: Relationship to beta-lactam susceptibility is reported; causality is not claimed.

column5: Class D oxacillinase; hydrolyses carbapenems
column10: Entry means a determinant was detected. It does not establish phenotypic resistance or its magnitude.

column5: Class D oxacillinase; hydrolyses carbapenems
column10: As above.

column10: As above.
